description: Per-job-type throughput, queue wait times, and execution times for the node's internal worker job queue.

panels.title: Current Job Latency (p99 Gauge)
panels.description:
**What:** At-a-glance p99 of how long jobs wait in the queue and how long they run once started.
**How it's computed:** 99th percentile derived from the job wait-time and run-time histograms over the last 5 minutes.
**Reading it:** Lower is better; green under 100ms, yellow to 1s, red beyond 1s.
**Healthy range:** Wait and exec p99 under 100ms.
**Watch for:** p99 wait climbing into the red, meaning worker threads are saturated and jobs are backing up.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:recordJobStarted / recordJobFinished

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(xrpld_job_queued_duration_us_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", job_type=~"$job_type"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(xrpld_job_running_duration_us_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", job_type=~"$job_type"}[5m])))

panels.title: Job Throughput Rate (Per Second)
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of jobs queued, started, and finished across all job types.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of each cumulative job counter over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Queued, started, and finished tracking together means the queue keeps up.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; the three rates should stay roughly equal.
**Watch for:** Queued rate persistently above finished rate, which indicates a growing backlog.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:recordJobQueued / recordJobStarted / recordJobFinished

panels.title: Per-Job-Type Queued Rate
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of jobs entering the queue, broken down by job type (top 10).
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of the queued-job counter per job_type over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Identifies which job types generate the most queue activity.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A single job type surging unexpectedly, which can point to a flood of a particular request or peer message.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:recordJobQueued

panels.title: Per-Job-Type Finish Rate
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of jobs completing, broken down by job type (top 10).
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of the finished-job counter per job_type over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Compare against the queued rate per type to spot which types are falling behind.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; should match the per-type queued rate.
**Watch for:** A type whose finish rate lags its queued rate, revealing where the backlog concentrates.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:recordJobFinished

panels.title: Job Queue Wait Time
panels.description:
**What:** Distribution of how long jobs sit in the queue before a worker picks them up (p75 typical, p99 tail).
**How it's computed:** Percentiles derived from the job wait-time histogram over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Lower is better; a widening gap between p75 and p99 signals occasional stalls.
**Healthy range:** Sub-millisecond to low-millisecond waits on an unloaded node.
**Watch for:** Rising p99 wait, an early sign of worker-thread saturation.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:recordJobStarted

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.75, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_job_queued_duration_us_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", job_type=~"$job_type"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_job_queued_duration_us_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", job_type=~"$job_type"}[5m])))

panels.title: Job Execution Time
panels.description:
**What:** Distribution of how long jobs run once started (p75 typical, p99 tail).
**How it's computed:** Percentiles derived from the job run-time histogram over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Lower is better; stable p75 with a controlled p99 is healthy.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent, but stable over time.
**Watch for:** Growing execution times, which point to CPU pressure or expensive individual jobs.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:recordJobFinished

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.75, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_job_running_duration_us_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", job_type=~"$job_type"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_job_running_duration_us_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", job_type=~"$job_type"}[5m])))

panels.title: Per-Job-Type Execution Time (p99)
panels.description:
**What:** The 10 slowest job types ranked by p99 execution time.
**How it's computed:** p99 derived from the run-time histogram per job_type over a 5-minute window, top 10 selected.
**Reading it:** Highlights which job types cost the most CPU time at the tail.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A job type whose p99 grows over time, indicating a slow or degrading operation.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:recordJobFinished

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, job_type, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_job_running_duration_us_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", job_type=~"$job_type"}[5m]))))

panels.title: Transaction Overflow Rate
panels.description:
**What:** Rate at which transaction jobs are shed because the queue's transaction limit is exceeded.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of the overflow counter over a 5-minute window, scaled to per minute.
**Reading it:** Zero is healthy; any non-zero value means transaction jobs are being dropped under load.
**Healthy range:** 0 overflows per minute under normal operation.
**Watch for:** Non-zero overflows, which mark heavy transaction load or a flood; note this counter is typically absent when the node is healthy.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp (job-queue transaction overflow counter)
